text:
nate: quick flag 1: we started a VPC hardening pilot in ap-southeast-1 (default-deny egress for worker subnets). seeing intermittent GPU warm-pool node joins fail with keystore auth errors. tagging @sara @sre-oncall.
sara: on it. can you paste the error from the node join logs?
nate: paste from node agent: `keystore: failed to fetch key session: HTTP 503 from keystore-proxy`
sre-oncall: likely the keystore proxy can't reach KMS due to new egress sg. which path are we using to KMS? privatelink or NAT?
kevin: this cluster was using NATGW to reach KMS via a shared egress subnet. the hardening removed outbound 443 to that subnet. node traffic is now blocked.
sara: ugh. that matches. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add an explicit egress rule for keystore proxy to KMS endpoint IPs for the canary, or 2) flip keystore-proxy to use privatelink endpoints (preferred).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created temp-rule-ticket #4872 to allow egress to keystore-proxy endpoints for ap-southeast-1 worker subnets.
finance: Note: if we go with NATGW fallback during spikes, estimated extra egress cost ~12TB/mo => ~$950/mo. Privatelink setup cost ~350/mo + per-GB fees but expected to be cheaper at scale and gives steadier latency.
sre-oncall: question: are these keystore calls per-node join or per-session? if per-join, the spike scales with concurrency when we spin up a batch of GPUs.
kevin: per-session KMS key is the new default for audit separation. node join path requests ephemeral session keys for each instance. so yes, join churn maps to KMS QPS. earlier sims show a 3x QPS at 100-node batch.
sara: for immediate unblock I'll re-open egress to the known KMS ranges (temporary) and add a cron to revoke after we finish the canary. also pushing a config to cache session tokens for 45s on the join path to reduce peak QPS. feature-flagged for rollback.
nate: canary plan?
kevin: propose: unblock egress, start a 10-node canary allocate, watch keystore p95, auth errors, and audit-ingest-rate for 20m. if stable, scale to 50 nodes. rollback if auth err >0.5% or keystore p95 > 600ms.
sara: adding monitors now. alert snippet: ```
- alert: KeystoreAuthErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(keystore_auth_errors[2m])) / sum(rate(keystore_requests[2m])) > 0.005
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
ops-bot: monitor-bot: monitors created KeystoreP95, KeystoreAuthErrorRate, AuditIngestDelta. Notifying #oncall.
finance: also capture the contingency: if we hit NATGW costs > $1k/mo we need to brief biz. adding to spend tracker.
sre-oncall: noted. watch for cross-AZ egress too 1: if the keystore-proxy ends up in a different AZ NAT path could spike latency. we'll add an AZ affinity for proxy.
kevin: I'm starting the 10-node canary now. posting metrics in 10m.
nate: thanks 1: keep updates here. if anyone sees unexpected audit log volume jump ping me.
sara: patched and toggled feature flag to on for canary.
kevin: canary metrics @10m: keystore requests +2.8x, p95 = 310ms, auth error = 0.1%, audit-ingest +8% (within threshold). scaling to 50 nodes.
ate: scaling. ops-bot: apply temporary egress rule id tmp-egress-6381 -> expires in 48h unless revoked.
kevin: at 50-node scale: p95 = 480ms, auth error = 0.25%, audit-ingest +15%. still under rollback thresholds. no rollback.
sara: filing a quota request for privatelink interface endpoints in ap-southeast-1 today. ETA 2w. if approved we'll migrate proxy -> privatelink and close the temp egress rule.
finance: good. please keep me looped on the privatelink ETA, we'll provision budget for the month of contingency.
sre-oncall: follow-up actions: - make join token cache default once validated, - add AZ affinity for keystore-proxy, - automate temp egress revoke post-migration. adding to infra backlog.
ate: thanks everyone. leaving the temp rule in place but documenting cost impact. close thread when privatelink migration done.
